Implemented on branch bug-1ef8-reviewbot-scratch (commit 01a2f473add0).

Plan review: PASS, signed, 0 blocking (verified_at_sha c57057f41, material_fingerprint 8944908dc75f1b8d). Two advisories, both priority-deferred:
- P6 ac-quality: two AC lines bundle deliverables with 'and'. Cosmetic; the criteria are each proven by a named test.
- T7/T5e: suggests an ADR 0112 addendum recording that enforcement now spans two callers. NOT taken as a file change, because adding docs/adr/0112-*.md to file_impact would invalidate the signed attestation and force a full re-review for a priority-0.0 advisory. The substance is captured instead in the docstring of the promoted gate_admission.scratch_unavailable_detail(), which names both callers and says why they must not diverge -- inside an already-declared file. Worth a follow-up doc ticket if the enforcement surface grows a third caller.
- G6 (dropped, low-validity): flagged that the predicate derives markers from REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR while the clone follows TMPDIR. Addressed deliberately in the docstring: the markers describe the HOST's declaration, not one consumer's temp path, so a box that declared a dedicated volume and lost it must not start large writes anywhere. Deliberately conservative, and it is what lets one predicate stay honest for both callers.

Shared check (AC5): the two-marker predicate was promoted out of gate_admission._require_scratch_volume into the public gate_admission.scratch_unavailable_detail(). _require_scratch_volume is now a thin caller that raises GateScratchUnavailableError; review_bot.low_disk.scratch_unavailable_detail() is a one-line forward. A test asserts the delegation by patching the owner and observing the review-bot's answer change, and asserts no module under src/rebar/review_bot names either marker literal, so the pair cannot be forked by string.

ADR 0069 treatment (AC2): the refusal reuses the EXISTING low-disk retryable gap reason rather than a new one. That reason is already in adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS (so under budget the voter defers vote-less with REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED) and it is the one reason ADR 0069 carves out of the fail-closed escalation, so an exhausted budget logs REVIEW_LOW_DISK_DEFERRED_EXHAUSTED and leaves labels unchanged instead of casting an LLM-Review -1. A new reason would have needed hand-adding to that carve-out branch and could regress into a false code veto.

RED evidence (AC3): before the guard, with the declaration present and the proof absent, the absence test failed with

    assert ['reviewbot-fej8aibp'] == []
    adapter: cannot identify the reviewed tree at .../var/gate-scratch/reviewbot-fej8aibp

i.e. the clone materialising on the unmounted mount point. The fixture pins tempfile.tempdir, not just the TMPDIR env var, because gettempdir() memoises its answer -- without that the absence assertion passes vacuously, which it initially did.

Gates: make lint exit 0, make typecheck exit 0 (758 files), tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py + test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py + test_api_surface_gate.py 55 passed after git add. complexity new=0 increased=0; mechanism new=0. voter.py held at 799/800 by folding the free-space alias into low_disk.pre_clone_refusal.

No infra/ files touched, so no collision with story 9183.

Landed as Gerrit change 2622 patchset 2, merged at 5932f4951b27 (no server rebase; the
submitted sha equals the reviewed sha). Both gates green before submit: LLM-Review +1,
Verified +1, 0 unresolved comments. Verified independently of the implementing agent's
report by reading /a/changes/2622/detail?o=LABELS.

WHAT THE FIX IS. The review-bot's pre-clone path did not honour the gate-scratch refusal
that story S1 (aa40) added for gate admission, so a box whose declared scratch volume was
absent would still clone the reviewed tree onto the unmounted mount point and cast a vote.

The check was PROMOTED, NOT COPIED. The body of gate_admission._require_scratch_volume
became the public gate_admission.scratch_unavailable_detail(); _require_scratch_volume is
now a thin caller, and review_bot.low_disk.scratch_unavailable_detail() forwards to it.
Two assertions pin the sharing because the divergence risk has two distinct shapes:
patching the owner must change the review-bot's answer (a copy would keep returning None),
and no module under src/rebar/review_bot may name either marker literal, so a future edit
cannot fork the pair by string. observability.sh is asserted to name the same constant.

WHY IT CANNOT BECOME A FALSE CODE VETO. The guard joins the EXISTING pre-clone admission
seam and reuses the EXISTING `low-disk` gap reason rather than inventing a second deferral.
That reuse is load-bearing: `low-disk` is already in adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS, and it
is the one reason ADR 0069 carves out of fail-closed escalation, so an exhausted budget
logs REVIEW_LOW_DISK_DEFERRED_EXHAUSTED and leaves labels unchanged. A new reason would
have needed hand-adding to that carve-out and could have regressed into a -1 cast over a
HOST condition. Proven by test_unmounted_scratch_exhaustion_is_terminal_no_vote_never_minus_one:
with the budget spent, status == "deferred-exhausted", votes == [], no VOTER_ERROR.

The sub-condition rides in the coverage block and message, where it informs rather than
routes -- and PS2 added test_the_refusal_says_UNMOUNTED_not_merely_low_disk after the PS1
reviewer fairly noted that the shared gap reason alone cannot tell an operator "disk full"
from "volume gone", which have different remediations.

TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING.

1. A VACUOUS TEST CAUGHT IN OUR OWN RED RUN. AC3 initially passed for the wrong reason:
   tempfile.gettempdir() memoises into tempfile.tempdir, so monkeypatch.setenv("TMPDIR")
   was inert and the clone went to the real system temp. The fixture now pins
   tempfile.tempdir directly. Separately, because TemporaryDirectory removes its tree on
   exit, a post-call listing alone would also be satisfied by a run that DID clone, so the
   fake records the live listing at clone time. This is the same "absence of execution
   reported as success" family as 9a17 and 90c7.

2. THE PS1 Verified -1 WAS BASE DRIFT, NOT A CODE FAULT, AND NOT A RECHECK CANDIDATE.

   "Extra 'grounding-terraform' is not defined in the optional-dependencies table". The
   branch was cut two commits behind main; c57057f41 adds that extra. Rebasing fixed it.
   Recording this because the failure shape (fast, uniform, install-step) is diagnostic of

19339 passed / 63 skipped / 0 failed. voter.py sits at 799/800 lines -- the free-space
alias was folded into low_disk.pre_clone_refusal() (one owner for both host disk
conditions) rather than adding a second guard, which is what kept it under the hard cap.

No --force anywhere. No infra/ file touched, so no collision with epic 6202 story 9183.

compiled_state.description:
## The gap

S1 (`aa40`, change 2620) put the unreachable-scratch **refusal** in `gate_admission()`, which wraps
plan-review and completion-verifier. That is where ADR 0112 places it, and S1 implements the ADR
faithfully.

But the review-bot's per-review clone does **not** pass through `gate_admission()`. It is a plain
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-")` in `voter._decision_for_review_target`, following
`TMPDIR`. So on a **declared-but-unmounted** scratch volume, plan-review and completion-verifier
correctly refuse while the review-bot keeps cloning onto the root filesystem, silently — precisely
the outage epic `6202` exists to prevent. A partial refusal is arguably worse than none, because the
loud half creates confidence the protection is in force.

This is a gap in the architecture, not a defect in S1.

## The trap (read change 2620 first)

An unmounted volume raises **nothing**: a mount point whose volume is absent is an ordinary,
writable, empty directory, so a naive `mkdir(parents=True)` silently recreates state on root and
every caller keeps working. S1's answer is two markers on two different filesystems —
`.gate-scratch-required` on **root** beside the mount point (the declaration, survives an unmount)
and `.gate-scratch-mounted` **on the volume** (the proof, vanishes with it). Only
declaration-present + proof-absent refuses.

## Approach

1. **Share S1's check, do not reimplement it.** Promote the two-marker predicate inside
   `gate_admission._require_scratch_volume` to a public `scratch_unavailable_detail()` on
   `src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py` (that module is not in the pinned API-surface baseline, so this
   is not a public-surface change). `_require_scratch_volume` becomes a thin caller that raises
   `GateScratchUnavailableError`; the review-bot calls the same function. One predicate, one pair of
   marker constants, so enforcement and `observability.sh` monitoring cannot disagree.
2. **Guard the clone at the existing pre-clone admission seam.** `_decision_for_review_target`
   already refuses before cloning when the free-space floor is not met
   (`if not _review_clone_has_room(cfg): return _low_disk_decision(), ""`). Add the scratch check
   immediately **before** that, and before the `TemporaryDirectory`, so nothing is created on root.
   Ordering matters: on an unmounted volume the empty mount point usually **passes** the free-space
   floor, so the scratch check must run first.
3. **Reuse ADR 0069's existing deferral; invent nothing.** The refusal is returned as an
   adapter-shaped decision carrying the **existing** `low-disk` retryable gap reason, built by a new
   `low_disk.scratch_unavailable_decision()` sibling of `low_disk.decision()`. That reason is already
   in `adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS`, so under budget the voter defers vote-less
   (`REVIEW_RETRY_DEFERRED`), and it is already the **one** reason ADR 0069 carves out to a terminal
   no-vote on exhaustion (`REVIEW_LOW_DISK_DEFERRED_EXHAUSTED`, labels unchanged) rather than the
   fail-closed `-1`. A new gap reason would have to be added to that carve-out branch by hand and
   could regress into a false `LLM-Review -1` on a host condition; reusing the reason makes
   "never -1" structural. The distinct sub-condition is carried in the coverage block
   (`scratch_unavailable`, `scratch_path`) and in the operator-facing message, not in routing.

Out of scope: `infra/scripts/*` and `infra/terraform/*` (owned by story `9183`, in flight).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — With the declaration present on the root-side parent and the proof absent from the mount
      point, the review-bot clone path **refuses**: `review_and_vote` returns a coverage-gap result
      and `clone_change_ref` is never called. Proven with the real two-marker files on a temp
      "host", not by monkeypatching the predicate.
- [x] AC2 — The refusal is an ADR 0069 **retryable deferral**, never an `LLM-Review -1`: under
      budget the result is `status="deferred"` with no vote posted; with the budget exhausted the
      result is `status="deferred-exhausted"` with no vote posted, no `VOTER_ERROR`, and labels
      unchanged.
- [x] AC3 — **Absence assertion (defect-seeded).** With declaration present and proof absent, the
      clone path creates **nothing** on the underlying (root) directory: no `reviewbot-*` entry
      exists under it after the call. Modelled on S1's
      `test_the_refusal_creates_no_store_on_the_underlying_directory` — asserts the directory does
      not exist, not merely that an error was raised. RED first: with the guard removed the same
      test shows the clone landing there.
- [x] AC4 — **No-op preserved.** With no declaration present (the default, and every developer
      machine and CI runner), nothing changes: the clone proceeds and no refusal occurs. Also
      asserted for the proof-present/declaration-absent quadrant.
- [x] AC5 — Monitoring and enforcement read the **same** proof marker: the review-bot path resolves
      its markers from `gate_admission`'s own constants via the shared predicate (asserted by
      identity, not by string duplication), and `observability.sh` continues to name that same
      marker.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py -k scratch -q` — AC1-AC5 on
  the review-bot clone path (refusal, absence-on-root, deferred / deferred-exhausted vote-lessness,
  both no-op quadrants, shared-predicate identity).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py -q` — S1's
  suite still passes unchanged, proving the extraction is behaviour-preserving for the gates.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py -q` — no regression in the low-disk and admission paths that share the seam.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py -q` — the three gates invisible to `make lint` (run after `git add`).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.

## File impact

`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py`, `src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py`,
`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py`, `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py`,
`tests/unit/test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py`.

S1's suite; it exercises the check being extracted and may need to reference the promoted public predicate so the extraction is proven behaviour-preserving for the gate path.
